Today's TL;DRRegimeRISK-OFF
Markets are in a broad risk-off mode as US-Iran military strikes escalate, pushing oil above $90 and threatening Hormuz shipping, while global bonds sell off (10-year US yield hits highest since 2023) on hawkish central bank repricing (ECB to hike, BOJ considers rate increases). The ADP August payrolls miss (38,000 vs expected) reinforces softening labor data but does not deter Fed hawkishness. AI-related equities (Snowflake, Nvidia) continue to surge on infrastructure spending, but the broader equity market is under pressure from rising yields and geopolitical uncertainty. Apple's CEO transition to John Ternus provides a defensive-tech rotation.

AI infrastructure capex surgeAI 基础设施资本开支激增
×10 · 40 steps
Hyperscaler and sovereign AI capex is surging, with top 4 CSPs capex up 87% YoY in 2Q26 and US hyperscaler capex projected at $940bn. AI and technology investment remains fundamentally strong despite macro headwinds. Compute supply growth continues to lag demand for AI services, with MiniMax's training utilization reaching 97% in 1H26 and Goldman Sachs expecting the imbalance to persist through 2028; Morgan Stanley estimates SpaceX's $100bn Starbase LA facility represents only 2% of total capex given AI spending scale, funded partly by ~$80bn/yr net debt issuance.

China Domestic Demand Weakness中国内需疲弱
×7 · 28 steps
China's domestic demand remains soft with consumer caution weighing on e-commerce (Kuaishou), catering softness (Foshan Haitian), a passenger vehicle down cycle with sales declining from 24mn to below 20mn units by 2028E (GAC), and broad macro weakness with manufacturing PMI at 49.8 and non-manufacturing at 49.0. Chinese consumer demand remains persistently weak, with retail sales growth stagnating at 0-1% YoY and industrial production capacity utilization at 73% in 2Q26. Despite Politburo and State Council pledges, these indicators confirm the continued weakness.

NomuraDissent5 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    The maturity of personal mortgage loans has been altered from 30 years to 40 years; the previous update was made in September 1999.
    c0993fe6e30b·《Structural policy changes amid sector downcycle》·2026-08-31
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Mortgage maturity extension from 30 to 40 years eases monthly repayment burdens and leaves more disposable income to home loan borrowers, but at the cost of higher total mortgage interest payments throughout the loan's lifecycle; with reduced monthly mortgage payments and unchanged rental income, homebuyers who have rented their apartments out may face more favourable net rental yields, in our view.
    c0993fe6e30b·《Structural policy changes amid sector downcycle》·2026-08-31
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    We believe the new property policies may alleviate homebuyers' monthly mortgage burdens, but is unlikely to have any direct and immediate impact on strengthening homebuyers' expectations about future housing prices, not to mention altering their expectations for job security and future income; the sustained decline in housing prices across most Chinese cities over the past five years and households' weakening income expectations should be regarded as two major overhangs on China's lukewarm consumption sentiment, in our view.
    c0993fe6e30b·《Structural policy changes amid sector downcycle》·2026-08-31
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    We see limited implications for the consumer sector from the new round of property policy changes; the property sector's dynamics (e.g., housing prices and mortgage payments) can change consumers' spending behaviours by shifting household wealth perceptions (wealth effect) and changing disposable income allocations/dictating savings goals (crowding-out effect), in our view.
    c0993fe6e30b·《Structural policy changes amid sector downcycle》·2026-08-31

Apple CEO Transition Marks a Unique Rotation into Defensive-Tech Idiosyncrasy
Apple stock rose 2.6% on September 2, bucking a broader market pullback, as John Ternus officially succeeded Tim Cook as only the second CEO in Apple's history. Ternus touted a 'phenomenal' product pipeline ahead of the September 9 iPhone 18 launch, and Apple's pay packages ($58M for Ternus, $47M for Cook) signaled smooth succession. Meanwhile, CNBC noted Apple's 2005-level decorrelation from megacap tech peers—investors are treating Apple as a defensive or idiosyncratic bet rather than AI-beta. The stock also tested $330 after holding key support above $300.

Goldman Sachs4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech emphasized the need for clearer improvement in underlying inflation trends despite better summer readings, commitment to a 2% PCE target, and that the policy rate is the "predominant tool to achieve the mandate"; the speech leaned against elements of the July FOMC that boosted term premium and elicited a reaction similar in shape and composition to the June FOMC.
    d5680b8d5768·《Back to Front-End》·2026-08-30
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Earlier and faster BoJ hikes to a higher terminal are steps towards long-end JGB stability, but we expect 10y yields to settle around 3% in the near-term with upside risks still alive until confronted with sufficiently benign inflation news; our terminal rate forecast is below market pricing and while we think 2.0% neutral rate is likely too high, it may take evidence of cooler inflation to convince the market.
    d5680b8d5768·《Back to Front-End》·2026-08-30
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    We now expect 10y JGB yields to reach 3.0% by year-end, from 2.5% previously, as we see room for the market to press term premium higher before gaining confidence that the policy path is sufficient to curb inflation risks.
    d5680b8d5768·《Back to Front-End》·2026-08-30

QDoes US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption cause oil price spikes and market risk?
▼ShortMiddle East Conflict and Energy Supply Disruption
BernsteinDissent4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Six months after the start of the Iran conflict, freight markets remain resilient: ocean freight rates are still more than double pre-conflict levels, while air freight rates remain around 30% higher.
    1377d90bd7c3·《Supply Chain Pulse Check: Solid demand and congestion supporting rates》·2026-08-24
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    The Strait of Hormuz closure continues to have only a limited impact on global container volumes, given that just 2% of global traffic transits through the route.
    1377d90bd7c3·《Supply Chain Pulse Check: Solid demand and congestion supporting rates》·2026-08-24
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    We expect industry supply growth to be +3.9% in 2026, before accelerating again to +7.7% in 2027 and higher at 12.3% in 2028; by the end of this year, the in-service fleet is some 48% ahead of 2019, with 15-20% net fleet growth across 2027-28.
    1377d90bd7c3·《Supply Chain Pulse Check: Solid demand and congestion supporting rates》·2026-08-24
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    DHL Express benefited from Middle East disruption, with volumes that would otherwise have transited through Doha and Dubai finding their way onto DHL's network; demand remains strong across all regions, not just on Asia-Europe trade lanes.
    1377d90bd7c3·《Supply Chain Pulse Check: Solid demand and congestion supporting rates》·2026-08-24
▼ShortMiddle East Conflict and Energy Supply Disruption
BofA4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    We expect MLCC book-to-bill ratio to decline from 2Q FY3/27 onward due to sales shortfalls caused by logistics disruptions in the Middle East and strikes in Korea, and the impact of advance orders from smartphone and PC customers.
    bbf3a99d0855·《Taiyo Yuden (6976): Shift from price gains driven by hopes on MLCC price hike to fundamentals: U/P》·2026-08-30
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Higher equipment utilization, with a recovery toward the 95% level, should increase MLCC profits. Even so, we expect the MLCC operating margin to remain in the low teens. Further improvements in productivity will likely be necessary for the share price to rise meaningfully.
    bbf3a99d0855·《Taiyo Yuden (6976): Shift from price gains driven by hopes on MLCC price hike to fundamentals: U/P》·2026-08-30
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    Underperform is premised on 1) a slow recovery in MLCC earnings, 2) postponed earnings expansion in non-MLCC businesses such as inductors and integrated modules & devices, 3) receding expectations for increased shareholder returns. While expectations are rising for an upturn in MLCC production trends as inventory adjustments run their course, we see limited prospects for a rapid rebound in earnings given weak final demand for smartphones and PCs. Share-price upside is likely to remain limited.
    bbf3a99d0855·《Taiyo Yuden (6976): Shift from price gains driven by hopes on MLCC price hike to fundamentals: U/P》·2026-08-30

  1. 1
    Premise
    4Q26-4Q27 strip-implied spot global gas spreads are up +40% vs the July update given the absence of improvement in LNG exports through the Strait of Hormuz.
    a5dfa7a6ce8a·《LNG Variable Cost Tracker Refresh: Tightening LNG Balances Send 2H26-2027 Spot LNG Margins Higher》·2026-08-30
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    LNG shipping rates from the US Gulf Coast to Asia remain elevated quarter-to-date at ~$2.50/mmbtu, higher vs the 2025 average of $1.55/mmbtu and the 10-year trailing average of $2.20/mmbtu; shipping costs to Asia have tracked ~$1/mmbtu above Europe given longer voyage distances of ~22-30 days to Asia vs ~15 days to Europe, plus tolls, congestion delays, and higher bunker fuel / boil-off gas losses.
    a5dfa7a6ce8a·《LNG Variable Cost Tracker Refresh: Tightening LNG Balances Send 2H26-2027 Spot LNG Margins Higher》·2026-08-30
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    The delivered cost to buyers of US LNG under long-term SPAs of ~$8/mmbtu (assuming a ~$2.50/mmbtu SPA fee and ~$3.50/mmbtu Henry Hub) now screens lower vs average spot JKM/TTF pricing implied by the 2027-2030 strip of $11.20/mmbtu average spot JKM and $10.80/mmbtu average spot TTF.
    a5dfa7a6ce8a·《LNG Variable Cost Tracker Refresh: Tightening LNG Balances Send 2H26-2027 Spot LNG Margins Higher》·2026-08-30

Rising Bond Yields and Geopolitical Oil Spike Trigger Broad Risk-Off Rotation
A synchronized sell-off in U.S. stocks and bonds pushed the Dow down over 400 points as 30-year Treasury yields hit 5.25% and Brent crude climbed above $90 following fresh U.S. military strikes on Iran. Wells Fargo and JPMorgan both turned cautious on equities, and CNBC's portfolio added defensive stocks to hedge AI exposure. Higher yields specifically pressure high-valuation mega-cap tech (the 'Magnificent Seven'), threaten consumer spending via wealth effects, and test leveraged AI builders like Oracle. The macro backdrop drove capital out of growth and into defensives, commodities, and cash.

XBI 63-day excess return +25.8pp (98th percentile of 10 years) · Market breadth at the 91st percentile (broad participation) · XBI +25.8% above its 200-day MA (94th percentile)
Thresholds calibrated on a single event — the 2026-06/07 semiconductor selloff (n=1)
Trigger rule details
The three observed quantities
Sector relative strength = how far a sector's return has beaten the broad market's over the trailing quarter (a price proxy for crowding)
Market breadth = how many stocks participate in the rally (equal-weight index underperforming cap-weight = narrowing breadth)
% above 200-day MA = how far price sits above its own 200-day moving average (the standard BIAS technical indicator)
How the light is decided
🔴 Red: hottest sector's relative strength enters the top 5% of 10 years (≥95) AND market breadth narrows into the top 10% (≥90) — both must hold
🟡 Amber: relative strength ≥95 but breadth only to ≥60; or either relative strength or 200-day bias enters the top 1% (≥99)
🟢 Green: everything else
Once red has fired, it doesn't snap straight back to green: it must exit the top 20% (relative strength) or the top 60% (breadth) before returning to green, resting on amber in between (anti-flicker)
Any missing data shows “No data” — it never defaults to green
